raw: 9.1 History and Rise of OSINT in the Intelligence Community[^47]
teaching_note: OSINT is an intelligence practice, not a synonym for everything visible online: a requirement, source evaluation and analysis turn accessible material into a bounded assessment. The CIA commentary is an institutional argument about OSINT's treatment, not a measured demonstration that open sources always outperform other disciplines [@ageint047]. Ask what the document observed, what its author recommends, and what remains a historical interpretation.
title: History and Rise of OSINT in the Intelligence Community

teaching_note: Read the 2024–2026 strategy as a dated statement of priorities for integration, tradecraft, tools and workforce, not evidence that those ambitions were achieved [@ageint048]. A strategy's desired capability, an implemented process and an evaluated outcome are three different claims. Its date range must travel with quotations; do not silently treat it as a current successor policy.
title: IC OSINT Strategy 2024–2026

raw: 9.3 OSINT vs. HUMINT vs. SIGINT: Comparative Value and Fusion
teaching_note: As evidence channels, OSINT uses openly available material, HUMINT draws on human reporting, and SIGINT concerns signal-derived information; compare access/selection bias, observation time and what each record actually measures, not a universal ranking. In a completed synthetic exercise, open notice N1 says a fictional museum is closed on 12 May, articles A1/A2 quote N1, interview abstract H1 explicitly repeats N1, and a supplied technical status summary G1 merely records its internal notice-display system as online; schedule S1 calls opening status unconfirmed. The origin graph yields one affirmative closure origin, three dependent repetitions, a different-property technical observation and one unresolved qualification, so fusion gives 'closure reported by N1; independently unestablished', not five confirmations. Removing N1 removes affirmative support, and correcting it to 'east entrance closed' narrows the result rather than preserving whole-site closure; different channels and different citation keys do not guarantee independence, including the same-URL strategy keys ageint048/301. These are fictional supplied abstracts, not collection tasks; use the record procedure in [@sec:analytic-workflow].
title: OSINT vs. HUMINT vs. SIGINT: Comparative Value and Fusion

raw: 9.4 Legal and Ethical Constraints in OSINT Collection
teaching_note: Public availability is an access condition, not permission for acquisition, automated extraction, retention, combination or republication. Separate applicable jurisdiction and dated authority, contractual restrictions, privacy interests and permitted purpose; ICD 203 supplies analytic standards, not collection authority [@ageint297]. For a supplied archive whose licence permits classroom reading but not redistribution, the bounded output is an internal record identifier and necessary quotation, not a republished dataset; if authority or rights cannot be established, stop that use rather than infer permission from visibility.
title: Legal and Ethical Constraints in OSINT Collection

raw: 9.5 OPSEC for OSINT Operators: The Sock Puppet Problem
teaching_note: The inherited heading names a risk to examine, not an instruction to build deceptive accounts. Distinguish legitimate separation of classroom data from personal accounts from impersonation, covert engagement and circumvention of access restrictions; this course authorizes none of the latter. Use supplied static records without contacting subjects or services, and stop if an exercise would require an account, live identity lookup or interaction.
title: OPSEC for OSINT Operators: The Sock Puppet Problem

raw: 9.6 Open Source Intelligence: Trends and Issues[^49]
teaching_note: Scale, search ranking, deletion and synthetic content can change which records are visible without changing the underlying event. Distinguish the exact captured version, publication time, acquisition time and transformation from the factual claim extracted; an authentic capture records a particular captured version, but does not establish that its assertions are true or that the record is complete. The inherited Academia.edu discovery reference is provenance for this topic, not sufficient primary evidence for quantified trends or current legal rules; those remain unsupported without an adequate dated source.
title: Open Source Intelligence: Trends and Issues
